label: Copy phase, 3rd+ output, when the fed-back input is r/y/n/e/g/j
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or at <DEL>), and essentially only from the third output onward (recall_idx >= 2 covers 99.9% of activations; recall_idx 0/1 almost never fire). It never fires on the first occurrence of a token, which follows because copy inputs repeat original tokens. Within that window the input token is the main gate: r, y, n, e, g, j have 17-24% firing rates (lift 3-5x) and hold most of the mass; u, t, s, h, k are weaker, and digits are low. Firing is more likely near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1 holds about 70% of mass) and in short sequences (L = 3-4). The strongest activations are at the last step of L=3 sequences, with input r/y/e/n as the second original token (e.g. s r k <DEL> s [r]). The predicate (copy phase, recall_idx >= 2, input in {r,y,n,e,g,j}) gets dev F1 0.60 and mass recall 0.81. Most of the missed mass is other tokens (s, f, u, t, k) near the end of the copy, and about half of the predicate hits are inactive, mostly in the middle of long sequences. So token identity and closeness to the end combine in a graded way rather than as a clean rule.
